Making both properties optional here lets TypeScript accept `fastify().route({ method: 'GET', handler })` with neither route location. I reproduced this on head baac6fb5 with TypeScript 6.0.3: the call compiles cleanly, but the same object throws `ERR_ASSERTION: The path could not be empty` at runtime. This is a regression from the previous required `url` contract, and the new positive-only type tests do not catch it. Please model these fields as an at-least-one union, for example `({ url: string; path?: string } | { path: string; url?: string })` intersected with the shared route options, and add a negative type assertion for the neither-present case.

This HEAD-only branch bypasses the `payload.locked` guard in `sendWebStream()`. With a `ReadableStream` locked via `stream.getReader()`, an explicit HEAD handler that calls `reply.send(stream)` now returns HTTP 200 with an empty body while the stream remains locked. `cancel()` rejects, the rejection is only logged, and execution still reaches `safeWriteHead()`/`sendTrailer()`. The normal path instead raises `FST_ERR_REP_READABLE_STREAM_LOCKED`, so this turns an invalid response into an apparent success.

Please apply the same locked-stream validation before cancellation and add an explicit HEAD regression test using a locked Web Stream. I ran the existing related HEAD/trailer tests (34/34 pass), which confirms this case is currently uncovered.

This new rejection test can pass without exercising any assertion when `addHook` stops throwing: execution simply falls through the `try`, and the `t.assert.fail` callback is never invoked. Assert the throw directly so the arity guard is regression-tested.

`fastify.redis` is not available when this options object is evaluated; the plugin creates that decoration only when registration executes. This therefore passes `undefined` and creates a new default client, while trying this after a completed registration fails because the non-namespaced plugin is already registered. This keeps the unvalidated value in the internal options while `getSecuredInitialConfig()` validates and coerces only a clone. The generated validator accepts coercible values such as `'true'` and `1`, so `initialConfig.lazySchemaCompilation` becomes `true`, but the route code's `lazy === true` check receives the original value and leaves compilation eager. Assign the internal option from the validated `initialConfig`, as is already done for `exposeHeadRoutes`.

A cached terminal build failure is ignored when a later code path resolves only one schema kind. For example, after the malformed-JSON request in the new test caches a serialization build error, a second malformed request reaches `getSchemaSerializer()` before validation; `lazy.serialization` is already `undefined`, so this returns normally and the route responds with the parse error instead of the promised cached build error. Check and throw `lazy.error` before testing the pending build key (this also prevents the public request/reply lookup helpers from exposing partially compiled state after a terminal failure).

Including `null` in this unconditional branch makes the new documented 304 path emit `content-length: 0`. The equivalent GET path leaves that header unset, and `onSendEnd` explicitly suppresses it for 304/204/1xx responses, so the synthesized HEAD response no longer reports the GET response's headers. The lookup key uses the literal string `undefined`, but `compileSerializationSchema` stores an omitted status as an empty segment (`undefined ?? ''`), e.g. `__application/json`. Consequently, once this schema has multiple cached serializers, `getSerializationFunction(schema, contentType)` misses the requested entry and returns the first cached serializer, which may have different metadata. Build the key using the same representation as the compiler cache.

Same change applies to `clientErrorHandler` and `frameworkErrors` in `server-options.d.ts`. Agreed the getter can't police every malformed shape, but it doesn't try to; its whole job is stripping the port suffix off `host`. While testing I ran the other invalid shapes through it: anything not starting with `[` already falls to the `split(':', 1)` branch and passes through as-is (`exa mple:80` comes back `exa mple`), so invalid input flowing through unchanged is already the getter's behaviour everywhere else. The unclosed bracket was the one shape that instead collapsed to `''`, which is the inconsistency this removes; no validation is added in either direction.

On `URL`, I did try `new URL('http://' + host)` while investigating. It throws on the unclosed bracket so it needs a try/catch, and for valid hosts it normalises: `EXAMPLE.com` lowercases, `bücher.de` becomes `xn--bcher-kva.de`, default ports get dropped. That changes `hostname` for well-formed requests too, which is a far bigger behaviour change than this guard, plus the extra cost in a per-request getter. If core wants strict Host validation that feels like its own semver-major discussion; happy to rework in that direction if that's where you land.

Agreed there are endless invalid shapes, but the patch isn't trying to catch them: it only removes the one slice where the getter itself manufactures an empty string out of a non-empty header. Everything else already flows through `split(':', 1)[0]` and comes back as whatever the client sent up to the first colon, so the missing bracket was the odd one out, not the start of a validation effort.

Going through `URL` would be a different feature rather than a guard: `new URL('http://' + host)` throws on invalid input so a fallback still has to be chosen, and it lowercases and punycodes valid hosts, so `hostname` would start disagreeing with `host` for well-formed requests too, on a getter that sits on the hot path. If core wants strict host parsing I'd treat that as its own v6 discussion; this change only keeps `hostname` consistent with `host` for the one input it currently mishandles.

With the new per-bucket `options`, `this.addedSchemas` is still a single global flag. This means adding a serializer-only schema will force validator compiler rebuilds (and vice versa), even though the corresponding bucket didn’t change. Consider tracking changes per bucket (e.g. `addedValidatorSchemas` / `addedSerializerSchemas`) and gating `setupValidator` / `setupSerializer` rebuilds accordingly.

`getSchemas()` now always merges into a plain object via `Object.assign`. This breaks compatibility with custom `schemaController.bucket` implementations whose `getSchemas()` returns a non-plain store (the codebase currently tests/relies on `Map` being returned, e.g. `test/schema-feature.test.js` "Schema controller bucket" uses `.size`). At minimum, preserve `Map` by returning a merged `Map` when the underlying stores are `Map`s.

The `addSchema(schema, options)` flag logic mis-handles the case where callers pass a single `false` flag (e.g. `{ validator: false }` or `{ serializer: false }`): it currently still adds to the disabled side. Since the new API’s options accept booleans, `{ validator: false }` should reliably mean “do not add to validator” (and likewise for serializer).

`schemaController.bucket` factory is now invoked twice per encapsulation context (validator + serializer). This breaks the existing contract that the bucket factory is called once per `register()` context (and is exercised by the current test `test/schema-feature.test.js` "Schema controller bucket", which counts bucket instantiations). It also gives custom bucket implementations no way to distinguish which bucket they are building, and doubles work even when the user doesn’t need the split.

Consider either (1) calling the bucket factory once and building validator/serializer *views* on top of it, or (2) extending the `schemaController.bucket` option to accept separate factories (e.g. `{ validator, serializer }`) while keeping the single-factory form backwards compatible.

The `requestIdHeader` section still repeats a second `+ Default: `false`` line just before the example. This is redundant and inconsistent with how other options are documented here; please remove the duplicate default block so the section has a single default value declaration.

This example now requires `fast-querystring`, but Fastify does not list `fast-querystring` as a direct dependency (it is pulled in transitively via `find-my-way`). In strict/non-hoisting setups (e.g. pnpm), `require('fast-querystring')` may fail unless users install it explicitly—please note that in the snippet.

In the `buildPrettyMeta` example, `Object.keys(cleanMeta)` will never return symbol keys, so the `typeof k === 'symbol'` check never matches and the example does not actually remove symbol properties as the comment suggests. Use `Object.getOwnPropertySymbols()` (or `Reflect.ownKeys()`) to delete symbol properties.
